beats.text: Ada Lovelace is usually said to have written the first computer program, in 1843.
beats.note: The algorithm she published was real. Whether it was the first is genuinely disputed among historians.

beats.name: Ada Lovelace
beats.role: Published 'Note G' in Taylor's Scientific Memoirs: a method for calculating Bernoulli numbers on Charles Babbage's unbuilt Analytical Engine.

beats.text: The Analytical Engine was never built, so the program was never run.
beats.note: Historian Allan Bromley found dozens of programs in Babbage's own working notes from 1837 to 1840: years before Lovelace's Note G.

beats.text: 'The Analytical Engine weaves algebraic patterns just as the Jacquard loom weaves flowers and leaves,' she wrote in those same 1843 notes.
beats.note: She argued the machine could act on 'other things besides number', including composing music: a leap Babbage himself had not spelled out.

beats.text: The first program is disputed. The first person to see what a program was for might not be.

beats.line: Maybe not the first coder. Possibly the first to see the point of code.
